# Basic French — provenance report

<!-- Generated from authored/french-basics.json by scripts/authored_decks.py. Do not edit: change the dossier and rebuild. -->

**Deck:** [`decks/french-basics.ttl`](../decks/french-basics.ttl) · **Cards:** 120 · **Licence:** [CC0 1.0 Universal](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) · **Compiled by:** Anton Wiklund · **Created:** 2026-10-04

120 basic French words and phrases for beginners: the numbers 0–20, the tens and 100, the days of the week, the months, eight colours, family members, greetings and polite phrases, everyday nouns, six adjectives and 16 verbs. The front shows the French word, nouns with their article (le livre, la maison; before a vowel or mute h, l' with the gender added: l'eau (f.)); the back gives its English and Swedish meaning, or the digits for a number, and for days and months a note on their gender. Words and genders from Wikidata's lexemes and the US Foreign Service Institute's French Basic Course (public domain), English and Swedish meanings from Wikidata where it has them and otherwise the authors' own, all checked against French, English and Swedish Wiktionary, the Lexique 3 database and Folkets lexikon.

## Licensing

The deck is CC0 1.0. Its content comes from two sources whose terms allow any reuse: Wikidata's lexemes and items (CC0 1.0: French lemmas, genders, forms, glosses, translations and French, English and Swedish labels) and the Foreign Service Institute's French Basic Course (Revised), a work of the United States Government with no copyright protection under 17 U.S.C. § 105 (five phrases with their meaning, and a check of four more). The selection of words is the authors' own. The English and Swedish renderings not taken from Wikidata are the usual equivalents chosen by the authors; several of them are the same short stock glosses that English Wiktionary, Swedish Wiktionary or Folkets lexikon give, as the method says. Single words and fixed greetings such as "see you soon" or "ingen orsak" are facts of usage, not protectable expression, so this does not carry those sources' licences into the deck; no definition, example, comment or list was taken from them. The rule applied throughout: English and Swedish equivalents and the facts in the notes not given by a content source are the authors' own knowledge, worded by them and only confirmed in a verification source. The backs that coincide with English Wiktionary's glosses are listed in its source record; two longer ones that matched it word for word (the back of pouvoir and a second sense in the note on je vous en prie) were replaced or removed in review round 3. French Wiktionary, English Wiktionary and Swedish Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0), Lexique 3.83 (CC BY-SA 4.0) and Folkets lexikon (CC BY-SA 2.5) were used for verification only. The Dictionnaire de l'Académie française and Larousse were not used, because their terms forbid automated extraction (method, step 9). So no source requires attribution or share-alike for the deck, although all are credited in its provenance. The quotations in this provenance report are not covered by the deck's CC0 dedication or the repository's MIT licence: quotations from the three Wiktionaries are © their contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0; quotations from Lexique 3.83 are CC BY-SA 4.0; quotations from Folkets lexikon are CC BY-SA 2.5; quotations from the FSI course are in the public domain; Wikidata data is CC0.

## Method

1. Who did the work. The research, drafting and cross-checking of this deck were done by AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic) at Anton Wiklund's direction, with machine checks against Wikidata and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators. Besides the authoring agent's own checks (quality control, round 0), the deck went through independent AI review rounds, also by Claude (factual accuracy; language and language tags; licensing, attribution and documentation; and a re-check of changed cards and a sample), each recorded in the quality-control log with its findings and how they were resolved. The cards have not yet been reviewed by a human subject expert (a teacher of French or a translator).
2. Word list. A candidate list of 120 words and phrases for a first French course was drawn up by hand from the brief's categories (numbers 0–20, the tens and 100; days; months; colours; family; greetings and polite phrases; everyday nouns; adjectives; verbs), choosing the most basic word for each concept, the same as the first authored Spanish deck where the languages allow. No frequency list or textbook word list was copied; Lexique 3's frequency columns were not consulted.
3. Wikidata lexemes. SPARQL query 1 fetched every French lexeme (language Q150) whose lemma is a candidate, with its category, gender (P5185), senses, English and French glosses and sense items (P5137). Six candidates were not found: quatre-vingts and five phrases. The lexeme search (API calls 2) found quatre-vingt (L10500, lemma without s) but no lexeme for au revoir, à bientôt, s'il vous plaît, je vous en prie, excusez-moi or de rien (je vous en prie was searched in review round 3, see call 2; it too returns no lexeme). So the five phrases on the cards without a lexeme are au revoir, à bientôt, s'il vous plaît, je vous en prie and excusez-moi; de rien, a sixth phrase without one, is not a card. The full JSON of the lexeme chosen for each word (the numeral lexeme for numbers, the noun lexeme for nouns, the adjective lexeme for colours and adjectives, and so on) was fetched with API calls 3, and the English and Swedish lexemes named by the senses' translation statements (P5972) with API calls 4.
4. Wikidata items. The items linked from the chosen senses (P5137), plus four items found with the item search (API calls 6: good evening Q19279366, goodbye Q2506912, hello Q12068060, thank you Q19279214), were fetched with API calls 5 (labels and aliases in fr, en, sv and mul). They gave the English and Swedish names of days, months, colours, family members, greetings and everyday things and the digit labels of the numbers. Where a sense has several items, the one for the card's meaning was used (eau: Q283 water; porte: sense S3, Q36794 door, not S1, Q53060 gate).
5. Phrases from the FSI course. For the five phrases with no Wikidata lexeme, the Internet Archive was searched for public-domain Foreign Service Institute French courses (call 8) and the OCR text of the French Basic Course (Revised), volumes 1 and 2, was downloaded (call 9). Au revoir, à bientôt, excusez-moi (Unit 1 dialogue), s'il vous plaît (Unit 1, classroom expressions, and a Unit 5 drill) and je vous en prie (Unit 2 dialogue, the reply to Merci beaucoup, glossed "You're welcome") were found with grep (call 10) and read in context with the English column. De rien does not occur as a phrase in either volume (only in sentences such as Je n'ai besoin de rien), nor in the FSI Metropolitan French FAST course, whose text was also searched (call 11). The deck's reply to merci is je vous en prie, the reply the public-domain course gives; de rien, the more casual reply with the same meaning, is named in its note rather than given a card of its own, since its back would be the same (the authors' knowledge of usage, confirmed by French Wiktionary). FSI's OCR text has no accents; the accented spellings come from French Wiktionary and Lexique.
6. Writing the cards. The front is the French word as in the lexeme's lemma (or FSI's phrase), lower case. Nouns are preceded by the definite article that shows their gender (le livre, la maison). Convention for elided articles: before a vowel or mute h the article is written l' and the gender is added in brackets, m. or f. (l'eau (f.), l'école (f.), l'homme (m.), l'ami (m.)); the apostrophe is the straight ASCII apostrophe, as in s'il vous plaît. Days and months are given without an article, as usually written, with their gender in a note. Colours and adjectives are given in the masculine singular with the feminine in a note; verbs in the infinitive. The back is our own short English and Swedish rendering of the main sense: for nouns the bare noun, for verbs the infinitive (English "to …", Swedish "att …"), for numbers the digits (tagged zxx, as digits are in no language). English and Swedish follow the Wikidata labels where an item exists and has them; otherwise they are the usual equivalents, chosen by the authors and checked in English Wiktionary, Folkets lexikon and Swedish Wiktionary (step 8). Where a French word has two everyday English or Swedish equivalents both are given (fille: daughter, girl; grand: big, tall; aller: gå, åka; aimer: love, like). Rule for text not given by a content source: English and Swedish equivalents and the facts behind the notes come from the authors' own knowledge of the languages, are worded by the authors and are only confirmed in the verification sources; such single words and short facts of usage count as the authors' own content. Where a back coincides with a verification source's gloss, the enwiktionary source record says so. Swedish backs are chosen in the register of the French: s'il vous plaît, which is polite, is "vänligen" (Folkets: särskilt i artighetsuttryck), not the colloquial "snälla" (Swedish Wiktionary: vardagligt) (review round 1).
7. Notes. A short note was added where it helps a beginner and is confirmed by a source: the gender of each day and month (shown for days with the indefinite article, un lundi, since le lundi means on Mondays), the feminine of each colour and adjective (nouvel and vieil before a masculine singular noun beginning with a vowel or mute h, confirmed by the French and English Wiktionary pages nouvel and vieil), un as the indefinite article, neuf also meaning new (with a front note "number" on neuf and un, and "colour" on orange), soixante-dix, quatre-vingts and quatre-vingt-dix with the Belgian and Swiss septante and nonante, quatre-vingt without s before another number, the pronunciation of fils, femme also meaning wife, homme also a human being, l'amie, la livre (pound), bonjour by day and bonsoir in the evening, salut and the tu/vous forms s'il te plaît and excuse-moi, de rien, Swedish requests ending with tack and snälla being colloquial, and the Swedish gå/åka distinction. Notes are our own wording.
8. Cross-checking. Every French word and phrase was looked up in French Wiktionary (calls 13): spelling, part of speech, the gender mark on the head line against the article on the card, and the first relevant definition (quoted in each card's evidence). Every word was also looked up in Lexique 3.83 (call 16) for spelling, category and gender. Every English meaning was checked against the French section of English Wiktionary (calls 14). Every Swedish word was checked in Folkets lexikon (call 17), English → Swedish, or Swedish → English when the first direction had no match, and, where a page exists, in the French entry of Swedish Wiktionary (calls 15). A Python script built the evidence lines from the responses saved during authoring, so each quote is what the source returned, with wiki markup and footnote references removed (the parsing logic is given with the calls); quotations longer than 160 characters are cut and marked with "…". The raw responses and scripts were working files and are not published.
9. Dictionaries not used. The brief suggested the Dictionnaire de l'Académie française and Larousse for checking the French. Their terms were read first: the Académie's conditions (https://www.dictionnaire-academie.fr/CGU) forbid "d’utiliser tout système automatisé ou logiciel pour aspirer ou extraire des données du Site", and Larousse's (https://www.larousse.fr/infos/cgu) state that it "s’oppose à toutes opérations de moissonnage et de fouille de textes et de données", including automated collection. Before reading them, the authoring agent had made a few test requests to find out how the sites work (Académie: the page https://www.dictionnaire-academie.fr/search?term=maison, its script /js/scriptAF.js, two POST requests to /search with term=maison, and the entry https://www.dictionnaire-academie.fr/article/A9M0242; Larousse: https://www.larousse.fr/dictionnaires/francais/maison); their content was not used for any card, and neither dictionary was consulted further. French Wiktionary and Lexique 3, whose licences allow automated use, took their place.
10. Machine checks. The dossier's Wikidata checks (the French, English and Swedish label or alias of each linked item that matches the card's text, and the mul digit label of each number) are re-run against live Wikidata by the builder on every build. Wikidata lexemes cannot be checked by the builder (it checks items only); the lexeme facts in the evidence were read from the API responses of 4 October 2026. The built deck was validated with the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators (scripts/validate_sources.ts).
11. Excluded: de rien as a card of its own (it means the same as je vous en prie, the reply in the public-domain FSI course, and is named in that card's note), words with two equally common meanings that a single card cannot separate (le temps: time or weather; la glace: ice or mirror; la pièce: room or coin), brown and purple (marron or brun; violet or mauve), words whose everyday form differs between France, Belgium, Switzerland and Canada beyond the tens noted on the cards (déjeuner, dîner, souper), the formal/informal pairs tu and vous (which need grammar, not a flashcard), the year (an and année, two words for one concept), and connaître/savoir (both to know).

## Selection

120 cards: the cardinal numbers 0–20, the tens 30–90 and 100 (29); the seven days of the week; the twelve months; eight colours (red, blue, green, yellow, black, white, grey, orange); eight family members (mother, father, brother, sister, son, daughter, grandfather, grandmother); twelve greetings and polite phrases (bonjour, bonsoir, bonne nuit, salut, au revoir, à bientôt, merci, s'il vous plaît, je vous en prie, excusez-moi, oui, non); 22 everyday nouns (house, water, bread, milk, apple, book, table, chair, door, window, dog, cat, town, street, school, man, woman, friend, hand, day, night, week); six common adjectives (grand, petit, bon, mauvais, nouveau, vieux); and 16 common verbs in the infinitive (être, avoir, aller, faire, venir, parler, manger, boire, aimer, vouloir, pouvoir, voir, lire, écrire, dormir, travailler). The list was chosen by the deck's authors for a first course, not copied from any frequency list or textbook. Every word has a Wikidata lexeme except the five phrases noted in the method, which come from the public-domain FSI course. Left out: de rien as a card of its own (same meaning as je vous en prie, which the FSI course gives as the reply to merci; it is named in that card's note), words with two equally common meanings (temps, glace, pièce), brown and purple (several competing words), words for meals whose meaning differs between France, Belgium, Switzerland and Canada, tu/vous, the pair an/année, and connaître/savoir. Nouns are given with the definite article; before a vowel or mute h the elided l' is followed by the gender, (m.) or (f.). Colours and adjectives are given in the masculine singular, with the feminine in a note. Days and months are given without an article and in lower case, as French writes them; their gender is in a note on every day and month card. Numbers are the standard forms of France (soixante-dix, quatre-vingts, quatre-vingt-dix), with the Belgian and Swiss septante and nonante in notes.

## Queries

**1. French lexemes (Q150) for every candidate lemma, with lexical category, grammatical gender (P5185), senses, English and French glosses and the item for each sense (P5137). POST to https://query.wikidata.org/sparql** (Wikidata (French lexemes and items))

```
SELECT ?lexeme ?lemma ?category ?gender ?sense ?glossEn ?glossFr ?item WHERE {
  VALUES ?lemma { "zéro"@fr "un"@fr "deux"@fr "trois"@fr "quatre"@fr "cinq"@fr "six"@fr "sept"@fr "huit"@fr "neuf"@fr "dix"@fr "onze"@fr "douze"@fr "treize"@fr "quatorze"@fr "quinze"@fr "seize"@fr "dix-sept"@fr "dix-huit"@fr "dix-neuf"@fr "vingt"@fr "trente"@fr "quarante"@fr "cinquante"@fr "soixante"@fr "soixante-dix"@fr "quatre-vingts"@fr "quatre-vingt-dix"@fr "cent"@fr "lundi"@fr "mardi"@fr "mercredi"@fr "jeudi"@fr "vendredi"@fr "samedi"@fr "dimanche"@fr "janvier"@fr "février"@fr "mars"@fr "avril"@fr "mai"@fr "juin"@fr "juillet"@fr "août"@fr "septembre"@fr "octobre"@fr "novembre"@fr "décembre"@fr "rouge"@fr "bleu"@fr "vert"@fr "jaune"@fr "noir"@fr "blanc"@fr "gris"@fr "orange"@fr "mère"@fr "père"@fr "frère"@fr "sœur"@fr "fils"@fr "fille"@fr "grand-père"@fr "grand-mère"@fr "bonjour"@fr "bonsoir"@fr "bonne nuit"@fr "salut"@fr "au revoir"@fr "à bientôt"@fr "merci"@fr "s'il vous plaît"@fr "de rien"@fr "excusez-moi"@fr "oui"@fr "non"@fr "maison"@fr "eau"@fr "pain"@fr "lait"@fr "pomme"@fr "livre"@fr "table"@fr "chaise"@fr "porte"@fr "fenêtre"@fr "chien"@fr "chat"@fr "ville"@fr "rue"@fr "école"@fr "homme"@fr "femme"@fr "ami"@fr "main"@fr "jour"@fr "nuit"@fr "semaine"@fr "grand"@fr "petit"@fr "bon"@fr "mauvais"@fr "nouveau"@fr "vieux"@fr "être"@fr "avoir"@fr "aller"@fr "faire"@fr "venir"@fr "parler"@fr "manger"@fr "boire"@fr "aimer"@fr "vouloir"@fr "pouvoir"@fr "voir"@fr "lire"@fr "écrire"@fr "dormir"@fr "travailler"@fr }
  ?lexeme dct:language wd:Q150 ;
          wikibase:lemma ?lemma ;
          wikibase:lexicalCategory ?category .
  OPTIONAL { ?lexeme wdt:P5185 ?gender . }
  OPTIONAL {
    ?lexeme ontolex:sense ?sense .
    OPTIONAL { ?sense skos:definition ?glossEn . FILTER(LANG(?glossEn) = "en") }
    OPTIONAL { ?sense skos:definition ?glossFr . FILTER(LANG(?glossFr) = "fr") }
    OPTIONAL { ?sense wdt:P5137 ?item . }
  }
}
ORDER BY ?lemma ?lexeme ?sense
```

**10. Phrase look-ups in the OCR text (lines then read in context with a small script that prints line ranges)** (French Basic Course (Revised), Units 1–12 (Foreign Service Institute), volume 1 of the student text as scanned on the Internet Archive)

grep -n -E "s.il vous pla|^Non,|^No," fsi-vol1.txt

    head = first line starting with ''' ; gender = {{m}}, {{m|fr}}, {{f}}, {{mf}} on the head line; pron = {{pron|...}}
    defs = lines matching r"#(?![*:#])", with <ref>…</ref>, image links, templates and link markup removed

**17. Folkets lexikon, both directions, and its about page (licence); entries looked up by headword and idiom; the matching code and the follow-up searches are given after the URLs** (Folkets lexikon (English–Swedish and Swedish–English))

```
https://folkets-lexikon.csc.kth.se/folkets/folkets_en_sv_public.xml
https://folkets-lexikon.csc.kth.se/folkets/folkets_sv_en_public.xml
https://folkets-lexikon.csc.kth.se/folkets/om.html
# index and matching (Python):
for w in ET.parse(fn).getroot().iter("word"):
    head = w.get("value").replace("|", "")
    tr = [t.get("value") for t in w.findall("translation")]
    idx.setdefault(head.lower(), []).append(("word", head, w.get("class"), tr))
    for idm in w.findall("idiom"):
        itr = [t.get("value") for t in idm.findall("translation")]
        idx.setdefault(idm.get("value").lower().rstrip("!.?"), []).append(("idiom", idm.get("value"), head, itr))
# each Swedish part of the back (split at commas, "att " removed) must be a translation of an English part in the en-sv index,
# or have an English part among its translations in the sv-en index
grep -n -E 'value="(hej då|bye|goodbye|thank you|thanks|tack|ursäkta|excuse me|varsågod|ingen orsak|you.re welcome|vi ses|see you|see you soon|vi ses snart|åka|school|want|orange|god morgon)"' folkets_en_sv_public.xml
grep -n -E '<word value="(hej då|tack|ursäkta|varsågod|ingen orsak|åka|vi ses|hej|adjö|god kväll|ursäkta mig)"' folkets_sv_en_public.xml
grep -n -E 'idiom value="(vi ses|vi ses snart|ingen orsak|ursäkta mig|hej då|tack så mycket)' folkets_sv_en_public.xml
grep -n -E 'value="(åka|ursäkta|varsågod|vi ses)"' folkets_sv_en_public.xml
grep -n -i -E 'vi ses|see you' folkets_sv_en_public.xml folkets_en_sv_public.xml
grep -n -E 'value="(snart|soon)"' folkets_en_sv_public.xml
grep -n -E '<word[^>]*value="åka"' folkets_sv_en_public.xml
```

## Quality control

7 rounds, 40 findings: 24 fixed, 1 rejected after checking, 15 needing no change. Every card's Wikidata checks (259 in all) are re-run against live Wikidata by `scripts/authored_decks.py check` before every build.

### Round 0: Sources, licences and machine checks (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — authoring agent, machine checks · **Scope:** All 120 cards: every French form, gender, English and Swedish meaning and note against the content sources and the verification sources; the builder's Wikidata checks.

Every card has evidence from a content source (Wikidata, or the FSI course for five phrases) and at least two verification sources. French Wiktionary and Lexique agree with the spelling of every French word; the gender shown on every noun, day and month card agrees with the Wikidata lexeme, French Wiktionary and, where it records one, Lexique. English Wiktionary confirms every English back; Folkets lexikon, Swedish Wiktionary or a Swedish Wikidata label confirms every Swedish back. The builder's Wikidata checks cover the French, English and Swedish labels or aliases of 98 linked items (259 checks), including the digit label of every number; they all pass. Discrepancies between sources and how they were resolved are listed below. No independent review round has been run yet.

French Wiktionary and Lexique 3.83, whose licences allow it, verify every French form and gender instead. | no change needed |

### Round 1: Factual accuracy (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — independent factual accuracy reviewer · **Scope:** All 120 cards: French spellings, genders (by an independent SPARQL query over all nouns, days and months), numbers, meanings and notes; the builder's Wikidata checks re-run live.

The reviewer found no factual errors in the cards' main facts: every gender matches the lexeme, every spelling and number is right and the builder's 259 checks pass. Three warnings and two suggestions were raised. The notes on nouveau and vieux left out that nouvel and vieil are masculine singular only and are also used before a mute h; the Swedish back of s'il vous plaît, snälla, is colloquial while the French is polite; the description credited Wikidata with meanings it does not give; and the checks on voir and nouveau confirm little. All were verified against the sources and four were fixed; the fifth needed no change.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| nouveau | The note "Before a vowel: nouvel" leaves out that nouvel is used only before a masculine singular noun, and also before a mute h; method step 7 had the same wording. | Verified: French Wiktionary nouvel "Masculin singulier de nouveau employée devant une voyelle ou un h muet"; English Wiktionary nouvel "used before a masculine noun that starts with a vowel sound", with un nouvel hôpital. The note now reads "Before a masculine noun beginning with a vowel or mute h: nouvel (un nouvel ami)" (Swedish likewise); both pages added as evidence; method step 7 updated. | fixed |
| vieux | The note "Before a vowel: vieil" has the same gap (un vieil homme; *vieil amie is wrong). | Verified: French Wiktionary vieil "Masculin singulier de vieux devant une voyelle ou un h muet"; English Wiktionary vieil "used before a masculine singular noun that starts with a vowel or mute h". The note now reads "Before a masculine noun beginning with a vowel or mute h: vieil (un vieil homme)" (Swedish likewise); both pages added as evidence. | fixed |
| s-il-vous-plait | The Swedish back snälla is colloquial and pleading, while s'il vous plaît is polite. | Verified: Swedish Wiktionary tags the interjection snälla "vardagligt". The Swedish back is now "vänligen", which Folkets lexikon marks "särskilt i artighetsuttryck" (kindly, particularly used in polite phrases); the note keeps that a spoken Swedish request usually ends with tack and adds that snälla is colloquial. Folkets and Swedish Wiktionary entries added as evidence. | fixed |
| — | The description says the meanings come from Wikidata and the FSI course, but for many cards the English and Swedish are the authors' own (round 0 says so). | The description now says "Words and genders from Wikidata's lexemes and the … French Basic Course (public domain), English and Swedish meanings from Wikidata where it has them and otherwise the authors' own, all checked against …", with the same change in Swedish. | fixed |
| voir, nouveau | The only checks on voir (fr label of Q25374341, en label "seeing") and nouveau (en label of Q15650394) confirm little of the meaning. | Looked up today (call 18): Q25374341 has the labels fr "voir", en "seeing" and only the alias fr "regarder"; Q15650394 has only the en label "new". There is no English alias "to see" or Swedish label to check, so no check was added; the English and Swedish meanings of voir rest on the lexeme's English gloss "see", English Wiktionary, Swedish Wiktionary and Folkets, as its evidence shows. | no change needed |
